Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

Research spike to determine the client-side follow-detection mechanism for the "Follow us on Steam" incentive. - [ ] The recommendation is confirmed with the user (decision gate) and recorded in this item before F4 implementation commits to a mechanism.
- [ ] Any unknown (e.g. whether a server component is acceptable) is surfaced as an open question with options, not silently assumed.

Success = a clear recommendation with evidence (docs/community/experiment) that the implementer can act on without re-research.

# Staff job-applicant specialization mechanic

## Problem statement

Main Street currently has a single staff mechanic: staff cards that go into the player's hand and passively expand hand capacity (`handSlotsAdded`). There is no in-game staff that is employed at a specific deployed business and grants that business a passive specialization buff. This item adds that new staff mechanic.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants more meaningful decisions when hiring staff: choosing where to place an applicant, weighing passive buffs, and taking on per-turn salary costs.
- **Game designer** — wants a reusable, deterministic staff-applicant mechanic that works with existing staff templates and can be extended with new applicant cards later.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Applicant trigger:** Each turn there is a per-turn chance that a staff member applies for work at one of the deployed businesses on the street. The chance is computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. The applicant targets a deployed business that has a free employment slot (one staff slot per business level).
- **Passive specialization buff:** Each staff member grants a passive, always-on buff to the business at which they are employed. Skills are assigned from a specialization pool and are randomized **once per game** at game start, remaining locked for the full game; a staff member's skill is disconnected from its nominal job (e.g. a "Baker" can carry a "Town Gossip" skill). At a minimum the "Town Gossip" skill is implemented, firing the existing once-per-turn peek mechanic (see CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN).
- **Hire / decline flow:** The applicant is presented as a new card type that **walks on from the left** of the screen. The player either lets it walk off to the right (decline) or hires it (walks into the hand / is employed). Hiring costs **no immediate coins** but adds an ongoing per-turn salary cost (deducted alongside existing staff/community-space ongoing costs during the income phase, clamped at 0 coins).
- **Capacity & let-go economics:** A business can employ one staff member per business level (level 1 = 1 slot, etc.). The player can let a staff member go (lay off), which costs 1 turn's salary and 1 reputation.
- **Tests & docs:** The mechanic is covered by unit tests (deterministic trigger under seeded RNG, passive-buff application, hire/decline, let-go penalties, per-level slot enforcement) and a browser/scene test for the walk-on/walk-off presentation. All related documentation is updated (code comments, README/wiki docs entries as applicable). Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Staff applicants for this mechanic are **distinct** from the existing hand-slot staff cards (`handSlotsAdded` mechanic) — they do not go into the player's hand as hand cards; they are employed at a deployed business.
- Applicant pool starts from existing staff templates; add new applicant cards via the follow-up work item CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK (not scope here).
- Passive buffs are applied per-business; must not conflict with existing per-slot `currentIncome` / `currentReputationPerTurn` caching in `applyIncome`.
- New card presentation must follow SLL positioning and the shared HandView/PileView / animation + SFX conventions per AGENTS.md (rule 8, `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, reduced-motion respected).

## Existing state

- `StaffCard` interface in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` (familly: 'staff') with `handSlotsAdded`, `reputationPerTurn`, `refreshCostDiscount`, `actionsPerTurn`. Staff templates loaded from `card-data.csv` (`_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES`).
- `MainStreetState.ts`: `streetGrid` of deployed businesses/community-spaces; `staffCards[]` (hand-slot staff) + `staffCardMarket[]`; business cards carry `maxLevel`/`level`.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts`: `hireStaffCard()` (hand-slot hire), `layOffStaffCard()` (hand-slot layoff), `executeDayStart()` resets per-turn state; `applyIncome()` in `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` deducts staff + community-space ongoing costs and applies per-slot income/rep.
- Related peek skill work: CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN (implement staff peek skill), CG-0MSXOWLHU0099QF6 (face-down deck rendering).

## Desired change

Introduce a per-turn staff-applicant phase/step in the turn loop: roll the applicant chance, when triggered pick a deployed business with a free employment slot and spawn an applicant card that walks on from the left. On hire, employ the applicant at that business, add its passive specialization buff to the business's income/rep/synergy computations, and register its ongoing salary cost. On decline, walk the card off to the right with no effect. Add per-level employment-slot tracking, and a let-go action costing 1 turn's salary + 1 reputation.

**Key Files:**

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — new state: applicant presentation state, per-business employment slots, employed-applicant list.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — new applicant-trigger step, hire/decline/let-go actions, ongoing-cost integration; `resolveIncident`-style applicant chance roll.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — apply passive specialization buffs per-business in `applyIncome` (+ currentReputationPerTurn).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — applicant/specialization skill type definitions (start with existing templates + Town Gossip skill).
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Town Gossip skill / any new specialization columns if added.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` + `MainStreetAnimator.ts` — new card type walk-on (from left) / walk-off (right) / walk-into-hand animation + SFX.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` / `MainStreetCommands.ts` — hire/decline input + command wiring.
- `tests/main-street/` — unit + browser tests for the mechanic.

## Related work

- CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN — Implement staff peek skill ("Town Gossip" active peek).
- CG-0MSXOXN81004MW8I — Add peek once-per-turn unit tests.
- CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK — Staff specialization: new applicant card suggestions (follow-up, out of scope here).
- CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4 — Group F: Staff abilities beyond hand slots.
- CG-0MS9HJ6AL0087DPB — Engine: ongoingCost for community spaces (same ongoing-cost deduction path).

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- Q: How frequently does a staff member apply? — Answer (producer): Per-turn chance computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20, recorded in comment CG-C0MT1CHYML001OOU8.
- Q: Are specializations passive or active? — Answer (producer): Passive, always-on buff applied to the business at which they are employed. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: When is the specialization randomized? — Answer (producer): Once per game at start, locked for the full game. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: Which staff pool for applicants? — Answer (producer): Start with existing staff templates; create a follow-up work item for new card suggestions. → Created CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: How is the applicant presented in the UI? — Answer (producer): New card type that walks on from the left, then either walks off to the right (decline) or walks into the hand (hire). Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: What is the specific applicant trigger rate? — Answer (producer): `(Reputation + income per turn)%` capped at 15%. Open detail: the "Town Gossip" example in the original description describes an *active* peek to the top 3 cards of the upcoming deck, which conflicts with the producer's "passive" answer — resolved as passive buff with the active peek delegated to the existing peek skill (CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN). Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20 + item description.

---

## Related work (automated report — find_related)

- **CG-0MLSDXY9F1FSGQ38** – Coloretto (set-building tableau) (completed)
- **CG-0MSRGUM4P009XRM3** – Upgrade level-up burst on target business (completed)
- **CG-0MSTB03U6009J2WV** – Main Street: clicking a tutorial button should not pass through to the cards below (completed)
- Repo file matches: `.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-0MSXIQDI4007K6N0-hud-2dp/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN-peek/docs/DEVELOPER.md` (contextual).


---

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-08-30: Planning completed by Map (herdr-downtime worker). Plan approved by producer ("LGTM") with one scope change: staff specialization buffs localized **per business** (Open Question resolved — "Move to per business staff").
- 2026-08-30: Six child work items created (test-first): CG-0MTFO4H1P00210PE (per-business buff scoping unit tests), CG-0MTFO4HGQ008VAQR (applicant flow unit tests), CG-0MTFO4HVS003ESVB (employment/applicant state + buff scoping impl), CG-0MTFO4IBI005C3GC (applicant trigger engine impl), CG-0MTFO4IQO005673N (walk-on presentation impl), CG-0MTFO4J6U003EBO1 (browser test + docs). Dependencies added (tests before impl; UI depends on state; browser test depends on both impl features).
- 2026-08-30: Description updated: ACs reworded as bullets, "**Key Files:**" bold section fixed per wl grouping convention.
- Gap analysis found the follow-up epic CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK (done, shipped) already implements the skill catalog, game-start randomization, buff computation, buff wiring, staff templates, and salary deduction. AC2 is therefore delivered; remaining scope = trigger, hire/decline/let-go, employment slots, presentation, tests/docs.

# Upgrade cards: consume an action and go to hand first (drag-drop = buy & play same turn)

## Plan Changelog

**2026-08-22**: Plan created (7 child work items, test-first ordering, Medium effort/Medium risk).

## Plan Summary

This work item decomposes the upgrade economy fix into 7 child tasks with test-first ordering:

### Phase 1: Unit Tests (test-first, no dependencies)
- **CG-0MT407BKP000J4N9** — Unit tests: upgrade action economy

### Phase 2: Core Engine Wiring (parallel with browser tests)
- **CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT** — Engine: wire action cost into upgrade commands

### Phase 3: Implementation (3 parallel tracks)
- **CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D** — Engine: implement hand-first click flow + target selection
- **CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7** — Engine: implement drag-drop buy-and-play
- **CG-0MT40HTYN008TJ6Q** — AI and Monte Carlo: budget-aware upgrade actions

### Browser Tests (test-first, parallel with implementation)
- **CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC** — Browser tests: hand-first click flow for upgrades
- **CG-0MT40GTSU006C6U1** — Browser tests: drag-drop and premium for upgrades

### Phase 4: Integration & Polish
- **CG-0MT42HHAB000VJUK** — Update existing tests, E2E, and documentation

### Dependency Graph
```
CG-0MT407BKP000J4N9 (unit tests)
       |
       v
CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT (engine: action cost)
    /      |       \
   v       v        v
CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D  CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7  CG-0MT40HTYN008TJ6Q
(hand-first flow)    (drag-drop)           (AI/MC)
       \                |                /
        \               |               /
         v              v              v
        CG-0MT42HHAB000VJUK (update tests/E2E/docs)

CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC (browser: hand flow) ---\
CG-0MT40GTSU006C6U1 (browser: drag-drop) ----/
       |
       +-- blocks respective implementation children
```

## Problem statement

Playing an upgrade card currently costs **no action** and never passes through the hand — a market upgrade click applies the upgrade directly to the first eligible business (`buyUpgradeCommand` → `purchaseUpgrade`, no `consumeAction()`). This diverges from the business-card economy (move-to-hand = 1 action, same-day place free, held-card play = 1 action, drag-drop buy-and-place = 1 action + 50% premium) and gives upgrade cards a free second daily action. Upgrades should behave like business cards: go to the hand first when bought by click, with drag-and-drop as the same-turn buy-and-play path.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want playing an upgrade card to consume one of my daily actions like every other purchase/play **so that** the action economy stays honest (1 action/day, 2 with General Manager) and upgrades aren't a free lunch.
- **As a player**, I want upgrades I buy to land in my hand first **so that** I can choose when and where to apply them (target a specific business, possibly next day).
- **As a player**, I want to drag an upgrade straight from the market onto a business when I'm sure **so that** I can buy-and-play in one turn at a +50% premium, exactly like business buy-and-place.
- **As a player**, I want to pick which business to upgrade when playing from hand **so that** I can respond to my current street layout (e.g. branches / multi-level chains).

## Acceptance Criteria (Parent)

- [ ] **Action cost — click path:** Clicking a market upgrade moves it to hand and consumes 1 action; playing the same-day moved upgrade applies it with no additional action; playing a held-from-previous-day upgrade consumes 1 action. All paths decrement actionsRemaining and legality gates reject the action when the budget is spent.
- [ ] **Hand-first + target selection:** Upgrade market cards follow the two-step hand flow — never applied directly from the market on click. When an upgrade is selected in hand, the player clicks an eligible business on the street to apply it; ineligible targets are rejected with illegal-move feedback.
- [ ] **Drag-drop same-turn:** Upgrades in the market are draggable onto eligible street businesses — drag-drop = buy & play in the same turn, consumes 1 action, and charges the +50% premium. Illegal drops snap back with feedback.
- [ ] **Free ops unchanged:** Event cards' free move-to-hand and free play stay free; refresh, sell, hint, discard, community favour, end-turn remain non-action operations.
- [ ] **AI + Monte Carlo:** MainStreetAiStrategy and MainStreetMonteCarlo account for the upgrade action cost in budget-aware valuation, and remain deterministic per seed.
- [ ] **Testing/validation:** New unit tests cover action spend + gating for all three upgrade paths; browser tests cover the hand-first click flow, drag-drop onto eligible/illegal targets, and action-budget dimming; existing upgrade tests updated to the new flow.
- [ ] **Docs:** All related documentation updated; full project test suite (npm test) and npm run build pass.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing action economy: 1 action/day (2 with General Manager) — upgrades must not create a second implicitly-free action.
- Same-day composite stays free (consistency with business cards); the 50% premium formula must match the business buy-and-place exactly.
- Undo/redo must wrap the new paths (snapshotted commands; new actions after undo invalidate the redo stack).
- State/transcript/save-load fields must stay consistent (e.g. justMovedHandCardId semantics generalise to upgrades; pendingUpgradeIndex-style state added if needed).
- Reduced-motion and mute settings must be respected by any new animation/SFX.

## Effort and Risk

- **Effort:** Medium (37.83h recommended, range [26h-57h])
- **Risk:** Medium (score 10/25, confidence 74%)

AI and Monte Carlo: budget-aware upgrade actions

**Priority: High** | **Type: Task** | **Parent: CG-0MT3IYSRL001VVUP**

## Problem statement

`MainStreetAiStrategy` and `MainStreetMonteCarlo` must account for the new upgrade action costs. AI upgrade moves/plays need to consume the daily action budget deterministically per seed. Monte Carlo simulations must model upgrade actions with correct action cost semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `MainStreetAiStrategy` chooseUpgradeAction: evaluates upgrade moves/plays against remaining action budget. Does not propose upgrade action when `actionsRemaining <= 0`.
- `MainStreetAiStrategy`: upgrade move-to-hand from hand counts as same-day composite (free) when applicable, costs 1 action when held from previous day.
- `MainStreetAiStrategy`: upgrade drag-drop model (if used) costs 1 action with +50% premium.
- `MainStreetMonteCarlo`: runSeed models upgrade actions with correct action budget semantics. Deterministic per seed — same seed produces same upgrade decisions.
- Monte Carlo strategy evaluation: upgrade actions scored against action budget constraints, no over-commitment of actions.
- Deterministic verification: same seed always produces same upgrade placement sequence and action spend pattern.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — action valuation, upgrade decision logic
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — runSeed, upgrade action modeling
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — actionsRemaining tracking in MC runs

- Updated `MainStreetAiStrategy` with budget-aware upgrade actions
- Updated `MainStreetMonteCarlo` with correct upgrade action modeling

- All existing Monte Carlo guardrail tests pass

# Intake Brief — Remove 'Market cycled...' activity log (CG-0MT5VXSSQ003O5ZC)

## Problem statement

Main Street's end-of-turn market cycling emits a noisy `Market cycled: N unpurchased cards moved to discard` entry on every turn. This adds little player value and clutters the activity log. The entry should be removed so the log only surfaces player-meaningful events.

## Users

- **Player** — reads the activity log to understand what happened each turn (purchases, income, events, gains/losses); does not want routine housekeeping noise.
- **Developer/QA** — validates log output against expectations; fewer spurious entries makes log assertions stable.

### User stories

- As a player, I want the activity log to omit routine `Market cycled...` notifications so I can focus on meaningful turn outcomes.
- As a developer writing log-related tests, I want no `Market cycled...` entry emitted during market cycling so tests do not assert on noise that no longer belongs in the log.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — No `Market cycled...` log entry.** Advancing a turn that cycles unpurchased market cards no longer appends a `Market cycled: N unpurchased cards moved to discard` line to `MainStreetState.activityLog` (including the N=0 edge case — no empty-market message either).
- [ ] **AC2 — Card cycling still works.** Unpurchased market cards are still moved to their respective discard piles and the market is still refilled via `refillSingleRowMarket`; only the log side-effect is removed.
- [ ] **AC3 — No regressions in log callers/tests.** Existing activity-log tests and other `addLog` callers (purchases, income, events, re-roll, incident-deck reshuffle, etc.) are unaffected; any test that previously asserted on `Market cycled...` is updated or removed.
- [ ] **AC4 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests verify that after a market cycle the activity log contains no `Market cycled` entry while the discard/refill side-effects still occurred (e.g. assert on `state.discards.*` and `state.market.cards` rather than on the log line).
- [ ] **AC5 — Documentation updated.** Any docs/comments that list `Market cycled...` as an expected log entry are updated to reflect its removal.
- [ ] **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Minimal, surgical change: touch only the log emission in `cycleMarketCards`; do not change cycling/refill semantics.
- No new dependencies or schema changes.
- If a doc or test explicitly documents `Market cycled...` as intended log output, that reference must be removed rather than left to rot.

## Existing state

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts:355` — `cycleMarketCards()` logs `Market cycled: ${visibleCards.length} unpurchased cards moved to discard` (neutral). The surrounding logic moves cards to `state.discards.*` then calls `refillSingleRowMarket()`. No other file emits this string (verified via repo grep).
- `MainStreetState.activityLog` is the append-only log consumed by the HUD. Other `addLog` sites (purchases, income, `refreshMarket`, `replenishIncidentDeck`, etc.) remain in scope and should not be disturbed.
- No existing test asserts specifically on the `Market cycled...` string (grep across `tests/` returned no hits); the closest coverage is `tests/main-street/MainStreetMarketCycling.test.ts` which validates discard/refill determinism. Doc references are limited to a code symbol mention in `docs/main-street/prd-multi-use-card-economy.md`.

## Desired change

- Remove the `addLog(... 'Market cycled...')` call from `cycleMarketCards` in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts`. The conditional `if (visibleCards.length > 0) { addLog(...) }` block should be deleted entirely; the discard loop and `refillSingleRowMarket(state)` call stay.
- Update any tests/docs that assert on or describe the removed log line (none known to assert today, but verify before closing).
- Add/adjust a focused unit test that exercises `cycleMarketCards` (or an end-of-turn path that invokes it) and asserts: (a) no `Market cycled` entry was appended, (b) the cycled cards landed in `state.discards.*`, and (c) the market was refilled.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — Remove the `Market cycled...` addLog call inside `cycleMarketCards` (around line 354-356).
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetMarketCycling.test.ts` — Update or add assertions that the `Market cycled...` log entry no longer appears while cycling side-effects still hold.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log.test.ts` — Verify no stale assertion on `Market cycled...` (grep today shows none, but re-check at implementation).
- `docs/main-street/prd-multi-use-card-economy.md` — Check that no log-entry documentation still lists `Market cycled...` as expected output (currently only lists the symbol name, no change likely needed, but confirm).

## Related work

# Show Card Position Outlines in HandView

## Problem Statement

Players have no visual indication of their hand capacity — they cannot see how many additional cards they can hold. Placing light card-position outlines in empty slots solves this.

## Users

- **Player** (Main Street, Golf, etc.) — sees empty hand slots as ghost outlines, knows instantly how many more cards they can buy/hold.
- **Developer** — enables outlines via a single boolean option on HandView construction; no scene-level wiring required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- HandView renders a semi-transparent card-sized rectangle at every position up to `maxSlots`, including occupied positions (ghost outlines behind real cards).
- Outlines are enabled via a new `HandViewOptions.showPositionOutlines: boolean` flag (default `false`).
- Outline rendering respects `reducedMotion` (no animation changes — outlines are static).
- Outlines update correctly on every hand mutation: `setCards()`, `addCard()`, `removeCard()`, `sortCards()` (animated path), and layout changes (`setSpacing()`, `setArcRadius()`, `setLayoutDirection()`, `setBaseX()`, `setBaseY()`).
- Outlines are destroyed on `HandView.destroy()` with no orphaned display objects.
- Unit tests verify outline creation, update, and destruction; a browser test in `GymHandPileScene` verifies visual correctness.

## Constraints

- **Visual style:** Stroke-only (no fill), 2px stroke width, colour `0x666666` at `0.5` alpha, shape `CARD_W x CARD_H` rectangle centred on the card position.
- **When to show:** Always — outlines appear at every slot up to `maxSlots`, including occupied positions (rendered behind real cards).
- **API:** Two new `HandViewOptions` fields: `showPositionOutlines: boolean` (default `false`), `maxSlots: number` (optional — total slots to outline). If `maxSlots` is omitted and `showPositionOutlines` is `true`, outlines render one per current card (matching the occupied-position-only mode).
- **Depth:** Outlines render at depth `index - 0.5` so they sit **behind** card sprites (depth `index`) but above any background elements. If Phaser depth sorting proves unreliable, use a dedicated render group.
- **Layout direction:** Outlines must handle both `'horizontal'` and `'vertical'` layout directions.

## Existing State

- `HandView` (`src/ui/HandView.ts`) manages card sprite creation, layout (`layoutCardPositions`), selection, drag-and-drop, and event emission.
- No outline or ghost-rendering code exists in HandView or related UI modules.
- Game state already tracks hand capacity (e.g., `maxHandSize` in Main Street) — outlines would simply visualise the gap between current hand count and capacity.

## Desired Change

- Add `showPositionOutlines` and `maxSlots` to `HandViewOptions`.
- Add `private outlineRects: Phaser.GameObjects.Rectangle[]` field.
- In `rebuildDisplay()`, after creating card sprites, create outline rectangles for positions `0..maxSlots-1` (or `0..cards.length-1` if `maxSlots` is not set).
- In `applyLayout()`, reposition outline rectangles to match the new card positions.
- In `destroy()`, call `outlineRects.forEach(r => r.destroy())` and clear the array.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — Add `showPositionOutlines`, `maxSlots`, outline rendering, layout updates, destruction
- `src/ui/constants.ts` — No changes needed (uses existing `CARD_W`/`CARD_H`)
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` — Add a slider/button to toggle outline preview
- `tests/ui/HandView.outlines.test.ts` — Unit tests for outline lifecycle

## Related Work

- `CG-0MS937FT9006273E` — Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight renders over cards to the right (completed; depth ordering reference)
- `GymHandPileScene` — canonical Gym scene for HandView testing

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep:** Outlines are strictly visual — no click interaction, no animation. Animated entrance effects are a follow-up.
- **Assumption:** Phaser depth sorting at `index - 0.5` places outlines reliably behind card sprites. Verified against CG-0MS937FT9006273E pattern.
- **Vertical cascade:** Outline positions must cascade vertically matching card positions — layout code handles both directions.
- **Empty hand:** With 0 cards and `maxSlots=5`, 5 outlines render (useful for showing the full capacity of an empty hand).

## Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "What should the card-position outlines look like?" — Answer (producer): As proposed — stroke-only, 2px width, colour `0x666666` at `0.5` alpha, card-sized rectangles.
- Q: "When to show?" — Answer (producer): (A) Always — all positions including occupied ones, as ghost outlines behind existing cards.
- Q: "Configuration API?" — Answer (producer): "Whatever you think" → per-instance `HandViewOptions` boolean flag (default `false`).
data.title: Show an outline of card positions in the hand

# Core engine: charge an action for event move/play
Wire the event move/play paths into the existing Main Street action economy. Same-day composite mirrors the business-card model (move spends the action; same-day play of that just-moved event is free). Coins unchanged (no cost at move, `event.cost` at play).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `executeAction` cases `buy-event`, `play-event-from-hand`, and `play-event` call `consumeAction(state)` before delegating to `purchaseEvent`/`playEventFromHand`. Legality gating rejects event moves/plays when `actionsRemaining` is 0.
- [ ] `moveEventToHandCommand` and `playEventCommand` each call `consumeAction(state)` *inside* the snapshotted action body (undo-safe) and expose matching `canMoveEventToHand`/`canPlayEventFromHand` legality (action-budget gate).
- [ ] `canPurchaseEvent(state, ...)` rejects when hand capacity **or** `actionsRemaining ≤ 0`; `canPlayEvent(...)` (add if not already present) rejects under the same budget and additionally respects the same-day composite — playing the `justMovedHandCardId`-equivalent event on the same day does **not** double-charge.
- [ ] Same-day composite tracking: controller/engine reuse `justMovedHandCardId`-style semantics for events (set on move, checked on same-day play, cleared on end-turn/day reset). Playing a held event from a prior day costs 1 action; moving and playing the just-moved event costs 1 action total (no double charge).
- [ ] Controller/UI: `onEventCardClick` and `onPlayHeldEvent` gate on `actionsRemaining`, spend the single action for a composite via the command/engine path, and no longer claim events are free. Undo/redo reuses `UndoRedoManager` and invalidates the redo stack on new actions.
- [ ] `npm run build` and main-street unit tests pass; the one-child-per-task state regression coverage is unaffected.

## Key Files:
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts`

## Target Outcome
Deterministic, fast unit tests prove `BankingGreedyStrategy` deliberately hoards vs spends correctly and respects legality, before implementation lands.

## Definition of Done
- Suite imports `BankingGreedyStrategy` (name === 'BankingGreedy', implements MainStreetAiStrategy) alongside unchanged Greedy/Random.
- Cases: (a) hoards (end-turn with actionsRemaining>0) when an unaffordable high-value hand/market target exists, (b) spends when no valuable unaffordable target, (c) at bankedActions==2 returns spend (bank value 0), (d) respects enumerateLegalActions legality (no illegal action emitted), (e) difficulty scaling — Easy spends where Hard hoards on same state.

# Feature: Design architecture & extraction script with history (F1)

Decide the target multi-repo layout, enumerate assets, and build the history-preserving extraction script. Full history preservation via `git filter-repo` is required (per producer).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Architecture decision recorded: core repo contents (`src/core-engine`, `src/card-system`, `src/rule-engine`, `src/ui`, `src/ai`, `src/balance-cards`, Gym, launcher shell `src/ui/GameSelectorScene` + `src/ui/createCardGame`, `electron/`, shared configs), game repo layout as sibling `tce-<game>` dirs, launcher composition via `configs/*.json` presets and a Vite discovery plugin.
2. History-preservation strategy confirmed as `git filter-repo` and the exact filter commands / script are documented and dry-run verified.
3. Asset ownership enumerated case-by-case for `public/assets/` — audit of `public/assets/CREDITS.md` and per-game usage; decision table committed (which assets stay in core vs move with a game).
4. Extraction script `scripts/extract-repos.sh` (or equivalent) produces the core-engine directory/repo and 8 per-game scaffolds from the current monorepo state with history preserved; dry-run output is verifiable.

## Technical Notes

- Use `git filter-repo` (not subtree/manual squashed history) — producer confirmed full history preservation.
- Enumerate shared vs per-game assets before any moves; thumbnail assets are per-game (each game provides its own).
- Sibling layout: core at `../tableau-card-engine-core` relative to each `tce-<game>` sibling.

## Key Files

- `scripts/extract-repos.sh` (new)
- `docs/extract-architecture.md` or decision record (new)
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
- `public/assets/**`

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: Full history preservation? A (producer, this session): yes, via `git filter-repo`.
- Q: Asset ownership? A (producer, this session): enumerate in F1, decide case-by-case.
- Q: Dynamic discovery approach? A (producer, this session): convention (GAME_INFO per game) is fine; per-game thumbnails.
- Q: Post-build dynamic addition? A (producer, this session): rebuild sufficient for now; Electron runtime plugin is a follow-up (core-version compatibility required).
